draft.title: What simple machines do
card: A simple machine is a tool that changes the size or direction of a force. It makes a job easier to do, but it does not do the job for you.
the force you put in to work the machine.
the force the machine has to overcome, such as the weight of the thing being moved.
Using less force means moving it over a longer distance. Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort. It has no unit. A value above 1 means the machine makes the force bigger.
draft.remember: A simple machine changes a force. Less effort means a longer distance, and mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort.

a.q: Which of these is something a simple machine can do?
opts: Change the direction of a force
Make the job need less distance and less force
Create extra energy for the user
Remove the weight of the load
a.why: A machine can change the size or direction of a force. It cannot cut both the force and the distance needed, because less force means a longer distance. The load still has the same weight.
a.clue: Think about what a machine changes about a force.

b.q: Sam lifts a 600 N crate onto a truck by pushing it up a ramp with an effort of 200 N. What is the mechanical advantage, and what does Sam trade for the smaller effort?
opts: 3, and Sam moves the crate over a longer distance
3, and Sam moves the crate over a shorter distance
0.33, and Sam moves the crate over a longer distance
0.33, and Sam moves the crate over a shorter distance
b.why: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 600 ÷ 200 = 3. Using less force means moving the crate over a longer distance, so a ramp gives a smaller effort over a longer path. Dividing effort by load gives 0.33, which is the wrong way round.
b.clue: Load goes on top. Less force costs more of something else.

a.best: Change the direction of a force

b.best: 3, and Sam moves the crate over a longer distance
